players.product: data-center air-cooled & water-cooled chillers, CDUs (1.3 MW / 2.5 MW / 5 MW) and Nlyte DCIM

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 results (CFO): reported sales were $5.3 billion, adjusted operating profit $594 million and adjusted EPS $0.57, with adjusted EPS declined 12% on lower CSA residential sales/absorption and China RLC weakness; organic sales were about flat; free cash flow was an outflow of $15 million (normal seasonality); company orders were up 11%, led by global commercial HVAC up about 35%.
quarterly_data.figure: sales $5.3 billion; adj. operating profit $594 million; adj. EPS $0.57; FCF outflow $15 million; orders up 11%

quarterly_data.signal: Data center demand (CEO): global data center orders were up over 500% and CSA Commercial HVAC orders up over 80%; CSA commercial order growth reflects some large data center wins in the quarter. The current data center backlog now fully covers the expected $1.5 billion of data center sales this year, and Carrier is targeting to exceed that number.
quarterly_data.figure: data center orders up over 500%; CSA Commercial HVAC orders up over 80%; backlog covers $1.5 billion 2026 data center sales

quarterly_data.signal: Data center phasing and capacity: sales are very back-end loaded, with most of the growth in the second half; Carrier still has capacity to take additional orders for this year and is starting to book a fair amount for 2027 (next year not as back-end loaded). The $1.5 billion data center sales guide was kept because of a big second-half execution hill, although bookings in hand plus those anticipated in 2Q would exceed it. CSA margins absorbed investments to enhance data center capabilities as Carrier tries to do more than $1.5 billion; data centers are accretive to the HVAC business.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 data center sales guide kept at $1.5 billion

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 outlook reaffirmed: sales of approximately $22 billion (organic flat to low single digits, now a bit above $22 billion) and adjusted EPS of approximately $2.80; an additional 2 points of pricing globally (about 75% related to Section 232 tariffs) offsets higher input costs, worth $400 million-$450 million for the year. Q2 guide: revenues just below $6 billion, operating margin of about 17% and about $0.80 of adjusted EPS; CSA second-half sales growth expected in the teens.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 sales approximately $22 billion; adj. EPS approximately $2.80; Q2 revenue just below $6 billion, margin about 17%, EPS about $0.80

quarterly_data.signal: CDU roadmap (CEO): Carrier chose to design and produce its own CDUs organically ("it's effectively a mini chiller") rather than acquire; it has introduced a 1 megawatt CDU, a 3 megawatt unit will be out in the third quarter or so, and a 5 megawatt unit towards the end of this year, maybe into early next year. CDUs have been sold to a few colos and Carrier is in great discussions with the hyperscalers; an expanded suite of CDU offerings will be introduced by the end of this year.
quarterly_data.figure: 1 megawatt CDU introduced; 3 megawatt in the third quarter; 5 megawatt towards the end of this year

quarterly_data.signal: QuantumLeap integrated data center offering (chillers, CDUs, Nlyte DCIM, building management with digital twin, air handlers, lifecycle support): since launching about a year ago Carrier has won $hundreds of millions in orders, which the CEO put at something like $300 million or $400 million, a lot of it in the CDU area. New products include two and three-megawatt maglev-bearing air-cooled chillers with free cooling and water-cooled chillers for high ambient data center environments.
quarterly_data.figure: QuantumLeap wins something like $300 million or $400 million

quarterly_data.signal: Two-phase liquid cooling: Carrier announced an expanded investment and partnership with ZutaCore, "one of the few guys that has two-phase solutions, which I think is where the puck is going"; on timing the CEO said two-phase is "not 10 years out, and it's not one year out" and probably within the next 5 years or so, while Carrier develops a whole host of single-phase CDUs; after looking at bigger plays it prefers organic development and VC-type investments, maybe with smaller acquisitions over time (in the $ millions, not in the $ billions range).

Commercial HVAC scale since spin: global CHVAC sales are up 80%, backlog up 130%, share up 500 basis points and margins up 3x. Carrier Energy is progressing with utilities and key hyperscalers, with gen 1 units to be introduced this summer. In China, Carrier is in great discussions on Commercial HVAC for data centers and expects some good wins; Middle East sales (about $400 million in 2025) were down mid-single digits on the regional conflict.
quarterly_data.figure: CHVAC sales up 80% since spin; backlog up 130%; 500 basis points share gain
